expected.description: Stronghold Europe is the full scenery-and-rules conversion for players who want Crusader's enormous skirmish sandbox in the forests and farmland of the first game. It is a different campaign mood, not a texture toggle, so PlayBound treats it as its own edition and keeps it separate from the clean HD and UCP3 installs.

expected.longDescription: OpenRA RA2 brings the Allied vs Soviet warfare of Red Alert 2 to OpenRA with high frame-rate rendering, modern netcode and community-driven balance.

set.longDescription:
Westwood's Red Alert 2 is one of the best-loved games in the Command & Conquer series, and this edition brings it to OpenRA through Romanov's Vengeance, the project by MustaphaTR that took over where OpenRA's own unfinished Red Alert 2 work left off. Allied and Soviet armies are here with their famous excess intact, and it goes further than the base game by adding Yuri's Revenge content as well.

Running on OpenRA changes the experience around those battles. You get high frame rates on modern displays, current netcode and an updated lobby, which is exactly what makes a 2000 game worth setting up for an evening with friends. The mod's developers have also taken liberties that the original never did, such as adding new subfactions, so this is its own take on Red Alert 2 rather than a strict recreation.

That makes it a good fit for people who want Prism Tanks, Apocalypse Tanks and a working multiplayer lobby without fighting an old executable. If you want the game exactly as it shipped, the differences may bother you. It is open source under the GPL version 3, and development happens in the open on GitHub, which is the best place to follow its progress.

expected.longDescription: Tiberian Dawn HD replaces the 1995 sprites with high-definition remastered assets, while keeping OpenRA's modern netcode and controls.

set.longDescription:
Tiberian Dawn HD is an experiment in having the best of both worlds: EA's remastered 2020 art, on OpenRA's engine and netcode. It is an official OpenRA project that runs Command & Conquer's first war using the high-definition sprites from the Remastered Collection, while keeping OpenRA's modern controls, lobby and balance. Multiplayer is still compatible with OpenRA.

The important catch is what it needs from you. The mod loads its art directly from an existing digital install of the C&C Remastered Collection, so you must own that game on Steam or Origin. Without it, there is nothing here to look at. A dedicated graphics card is recommended too, because all those high-resolution assets are heavy.

The project's own readme is candid about its status. It calls itself a prototype and a proof of concept, says performance, memory use and loading times have not been optimised, and warns you to proceed at your own risk. So treat this as a good-looking curiosity for owners of the Remastered Collection, rather than the stable way to play. For that, the official OpenRA edition is the better choice. It is open source under the GPL version 3, but no formal releases have been published.

expected.longDescription: VoxeLibre, the successor to MineClone2, is a Minecraft-inspired survival sandbox for Luanti. It is released under free licenses with no storefront or monetisation, and offers survival, building, farming and exploration.

set.longDescription:
VoxeLibre is the survival sandbox most people find first on Luanti, and with close to 800,000 downloads on ContentDB, it is easy to see why. Formerly called MineClone2, it was inspired by Minecraft and forked from an earlier project called MineClone before being renamed and substantially expanded. If you have played Minecraft, you already know what to do when the first night falls.

The familiar pieces are all here: survival and creative modes, hostile mobs, mining and ores, and farming, along with enchanting, redstone circuits, minecarts and Nether portals. It has also begun to add ideas of its own instead of simply following its inspiration, which separates it from stricter recreations such as Mineclonia, also listed here.

It remains officially in beta, described by its maintainers as fully playable but not yet feature-complete, so expect a few gaps next to the game that inspired it. In exchange you get something free, open and very moddable, with no storefront, available in about 21 languages and rated very positively by its players. Its code is GPL and its media is under Creative Commons. PlayBound installs Luanti with VoxeLibre already in place, so there is no setting up to do before your first shelter.

expected.longDescription: Exile throws players into an unforgiving wilderness where temperature, nutrition, thirst and wildlife are real threats. Advancement is slow and survival is the point.

set.longDescription:
Exile is the block game for people who think survival games are too polite. Created by Dokimi and now developed by the Exile Team, it drops you into the wilderness as an outcast with no tools and little hope, and its own listing calls it challenging and at times brutal. There is no gentle first night here: the cold, your hunger and your body will all work against you from the first minute.

Finding food, water and shelter is the whole early game. You craft basic tools, then work up through fires, kilns and furnaces, and the technology stays simple, because progress is measured in staying alive. Hypothermia, exhaustion and disease are all things that can kill you, while seasonal weather, erosion and water that flows through soil make the world feel like a place with no interest in you.

For a harder and slower game, the Carpathian map generator is supported alongside the standard Valleys setting. It is free software on Luanti, with no required add-ons, and it is actively developed. Its developers warn that some people may find parts of it difficult or disturbing, which is fair. Choose it if you want every campfire you survive to feel like an achievement.

expected.longDescription: NodeCore is a puzzle-survival game with no text prompts, crafting menu or GUI windows. Everything is learned by experimenting with the world, so progress feels like discovery.

set.longDescription:
NodeCore is one of the strangest games on Luanti, and that is the reason to play it. Warr1024's game calls itself a surreal dream-world where everything is possible but nothing is easy. It throws out the things block games normally rely on: there is no crafting grid and almost no explanation, so you learn how the world works by pounding on it, moving things around and paying attention to what happens.

All crafting happens in the world itself rather than in a menu. Stack the right things in the right place and strike them, and something new may appear. From those odd beginnings it goes much further than you would expect, with machines built from separate parts, hinged and rotary machinery, automated crafting and even logic circuits that work with light.

Its listing warns of a different kind of difficulty, and that is accurate. There are no monsters to blame, only your own understanding, and progress comes from discovery. It has a built-in new player guide, plays alone or with others, and works with a gamepad or on mobile. The whole thing is a tiny download of about 1.4 MB under the MIT license, and it has been in active development since 2019. Try it if figuring things out is your favourite part of any game.

expected.longDescription: Asuna is a gentle, exploration-focused voxel RPG with custom biomes, plants, wildlife and building materials.

set.longDescription:
Asuna is the Luanti game to install if you mostly want somewhere beautiful to wander. EmptyStar has blended many of the platform's best biome and decoration mods into one curated package, and the numbers show how much that adds up to: more than 60 biomes, over 100 flowers, plants and mushrooms, more than 30 farming crops, 27 animals and creatures, and 80 decorative stones to build with.

It leaves the tone up to you, through content packs that can be switched on or off in settings. Nutrition rewards a good diet with faster movement and health regeneration, and starvation is off by default. Wayfarer adds achievements, loot chests and Worldgates, a teleportation network for getting around all that land. Menagerie brings the animals and slimes, Stratosphere adds sky islands and harvestable clouds, and Research offers an earned creative mode, where discovering an item lets you duplicate it.

With 54 achievements and 31 background music tracks, it feels more complete than its peaceful pitch suggests. Mapgen v7 is the only officially supported map generator, and it is the one that produces those sky islands. It is free software, rated very positively by players, and a gentle counterweight to the harsher survival games in this family.

expected.longDescription: A long-running fork of Shattered Pixel Dungeon that expands well past the original with extra classes, more items and a much longer set of challenges.

set.longDescription:
Rat King Adventure is what happens when a joke mod's own joke mod keeps growing. It is an expansive fork of RKPD2, which is itself built on Shattered Pixel Dungeon, and it stays in sync with updates from both. Where Shattered ends, this one keeps going: past Yog lies the Abyss, a new area of tough enemies with no set end, for anybody who thought the final boss should have been a starting point.

The additions are as wild as that suggests. Tier-6 weapons have unusual effects, expanded talents reach tier 4, and every class has secret subclasses to find. Rats also turn up in place of some common enemies. Kromers are unpredictable items with high risk and high reward, special seeds grant unique effects or whole new mechanics, and new challenges build on the existing ones if you somehow still need a harder time.

Nobody should start here. It assumes you already know Shattered's rules and want them stretched until they snap, and the balance is firmly on the side of fun. It installs and saves separately, so it never disturbs a normal Shattered run, and PlayBound installs a Java runtime on desktop if you need one. It is free under the GPL version 3, on Android and desktop.

expected.longDescription: Frontier Station turns SS14 into an open-universe sandbox RPG where players own starships, mine asteroids and explore.

set.longDescription:
Frontier Station takes Space Station 14 out of the station. The original game is a round-based social disaster about one crew, one station and everything that goes wrong; this fork of it, running on the same Robust Toolbox engine, turns that into an open-universe sandbox where you own a ship and decide for yourself what to do with it.

Instead of a job assignment, you get a career of your own making. Players buy personal starships, then mine asteroid belts, explore abandoned derelicts and trade across orbital stations. The detailed simulation that makes Space Station 14 so memorable all carries over, including atmospherics, power and medical systems, so a hull breach on your own little freighter is a much more personal problem than one on a big station.

That makes it a slower and more self-directed game than the base experience, with less of the paranoia and more room for long sessions with friends on a shared ship. It also shares SS14's learning curve, so expect to spend your first hours confused and probably on fire. Frontier has its own wiki for its ships and systems, and its code is open on GitHub. Join through the Space Station 14 launcher, and find a crew if you can.
